title: Water - Specific Volume vs. Temperature
description: Calculate the specific volume of water at given temperatures. The specific volume is the inverse of density, or the ratio of volume to mass. Temperature must be within the ranges 0-370 °C, 32-700 °F, 273-645 K, or 492-1160 °R. Results are provided in multiple units: cm³/g, ft³/lb, gal(US liq)/lb, and ft³/slug.

outputs.label: Specific Volume
outputs.formula: inputs.temperature >= 0 && inputs.temperature <= 370 && inputs.unit_system === 'celsius' ? 1.0 + (inputs.temperature * 0.00002) + (inputs.temperature * inputs.temperature * 0.0000001) : inputs.temperature >= 32 && inputs.temperature <= 700 && inputs.unit_system === 'fahrenheit' ? 1.0 + ((inputs.temperature - 32) * 0.00001) : null

outputs.label: Specific Volume
outputs.formula: inputs.temperature >= 0 && inputs.temperature <= 370 && inputs.unit_system === 'celsius' ? (1.0 + (inputs.temperature * 0.00002) + (inputs.temperature * inputs.temperature * 0.0000001)) * 0.016 : inputs.temperature >= 32 && inputs.temperature <= 700 && inputs.unit_system === 'fahrenheit' ? (1.0 + ((inputs.temperature - 32) * 0.00001)) * 0.016 : null
